title.en: It Is Well with My Soul

headline.en: It Is Well with My Soul: hear the whole song first, then the tune on its own.

detail.en: The whole song, every part together
The guide sings it, line by line
Stop if anything tightens or hurts

headline.en: Now the tune on its own.

detail.en: Follow the words as it plays

text.en: Find the notes of line 1: each one waits until you're on it.
This hymn was first printed in 1876, as No. 76 in Gospel Hymns No. 2, the songbook Philip Bliss and Ira Sankey made for their revival meetings. These are Bliss's own four parts from that page.

source.en: Gospel Hymns No. 2 (1876), No. 76, read from the scan

text.en: Hear line 1, then sing it back.
Hear line 2, then sing it back.
Now lines 1 and 2 joined, with the guide.
Hear line 3, then sing it back.
Hear line 4, then sing it back.
Now lines 3 and 4 joined, with the guide.
Hear line 5, then sing it back.
Line 6 is the tune of line 5 again, with new words. Sing it with the guide.
Hear line 7, then sing it back.
Now lines 5 to 7 joined, with the guide.
Verse 1 start to end, with the guide.
Chorus start to end, with the guide.
The whole song, with the guide.
Sing your part with the other parts, and the guide with you. Hold your line while the others move.
The guide drops out: your part with the others only. Give me my note plays your first note quietly.
Once more on your own, from the top.
Record the tune of It Is Well with My Soul in Sing, with the other parts playing.
In the chorus the tune holds "well" and "soul" while the other parts answer "it is well" underneath: Bliss wrote the echo into the parts himself.
